source_excerpts.text:
## 4. Convert relative class weights into relative logical reliability

Let the matching counter approximate each calibrated class weight within \(1\pm\eta\), and select the larger estimate. Define
\[
\rho=e^{2\Gamma}\frac{1+\eta}{1-\eta}.
\]

On simultaneous calibration and counting success,
\[
\boxed{
r_{\mathrm{selected}}(s)\le \rho\,r_*(s),
\qquad
r_*(s)=\frac{\min(Z_0,Z_1)}{Z_0+Z_1}.
}
\tag{12}
\]

The proof is short. If the estimated winner is correct, the decoder is Bayes-optimal. If it is wrong, the true winning class can exceed the selected class by at most \(\rho\). Since the two corresponding failure probabilities have the same denominator, their ratio is at most \(\rho\).

This controls the **failure probability itself**, rather than an additive error that could overwhelm an exponentially small target.

### The decoder’s own failure probability must also be paid

A fixed confidence such as \(99\%\) would be unacceptable when \(r_*(s)\) is tiny.

If both sectors are feasible, each contains a fault history of probability at least \(p_{\min}^m\). Since \(\Pr(s)\le1\),
\[
r_*(s)\ge p_{\min}^m.
\tag{13}
\]

Choose calibration and counter confidence so that
\[
\delta_{\mathrm{total}}
\le \frac{\varepsilon}{2}p_{\min}^m,
\qquad
\rho\le1+\frac{\varepsilon}{2}.
\]
Then
\[
\boxed{
\mathbb E_{\mathrm{calibration,algorithm}}
r_{\mathrm{selected}}(s)
\le(1+\varepsilon)r_*(s).
}
\tag{14}
\]

The confidence cost is only
\[
\log\delta_{\mathrm{total}}^{-1}
=
O\!\left(m\log p_{\min}^{-1}
+\log\varepsilon^{-1}\right).
\tag{15}
\]

Zero sectors are handled by exact matching feasibility. For supplied rational rates, the sharper floor \(\prod_e\min(p_e,1-p_e)\) can replace \(p_{\min}^m\).

The same weight intervals give a confidence interval for the chosen decoder’s conditional failure. If \(L_h\le Z_h\le U_h\), its risk lies in
\[
\left[
\frac{L_{1-h}}{L_{1-h}+U_h},
\frac{U_{1-h}}{U_{1-h}+L_h}
\right].
\tag{16}
\]
Its endpoint ratio is at most \(\rho^2\), so the budgets can be chosen to make that ratio at most \(1+\varepsilon\).

Under the stated Pauli model, this also controls the actual logical measurement instrument: its diamond distance from ideal logical readout with the same syndrome record is \(2\mathbb E_s r(s)\). The conclusion applies to unknown logical inputs, including inputs entangled with a reference.

statement: Relative class weights give near-Bayes risk only after the algorithm own failure probability is budgeted at the logical-error scale.
